title: Local Snapshot Agent for Jurisdictional Proof & Immutable Archive
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) need an auditable, jurisdiction-aware snapshot of control artifacts (logs, config snapshots, audit events, evidence manifests) that satisfies SOC 2 / ISO 27001 auditors without requiring full data duplication across regions.

Goal: Build a lightweight Local Snapshot Agent that runs in customer-controlled environments and produces signed, append-only proof manifests plus optional content snapshots. The agent should produce immutable proof artifacts (signed manifests + checksums) that can be pushed to an on-prem immutable store or to Redwood-managed ledger (for customers that opt in). It must support jurisdictional retention rules (retain full snapshots only in allowed regions; keep concise signed proof manifests for longer retention across geographies).

Key requirements and constraints:
- Runs as a small daemon/container in customer VPC or on-prem host; minimal footprint and predictable disk usage.
- Produces periodic manifests capturing: file-level checksums, object references (S3/GCS path or local path), metadata (timestamp, agent id, region tag, KMS key id), and cryptographic signature.
- Supports content deduplication and chunk-level checksums for large artifacts (model shards, datasets).
- Integrates with customer KMS/HSM for envelope encryption of snapshots and uses Redwood service key to sign proofs only when customer allows cross-region proof storage.
- Enforces retention policy at two tiers: snapshot retention (may be jurisdiction-limited) and proof-manifest retention (globally retained as immutable ledger entries).
- Exposes an ingestion API for Redwood evidence-synthesizer to pull manifests; supports push to RedLedger or push to customer immutable store (e.g., S3 ObjectLock, on-prem NVM with WORM).
- Observable: metrics for snapshot duration, bytes processed, failed-signatures, disk pressure; logs for audit; healthcheck endpoints.
- Operational safety: backpressure when network constrained, configurable bandwidth cap, graceful aborts on low-disk thresholds, retry/exponential backoff for uploads.

Non-goals: full content archival on Redwood-side for all customers (we'll support opt-in), replacing existing log-collector agents used by customers today.

Implementation notes / design decisions so far:
- Agent written in Go to minimize runtime dependencies; binary + small config file.
- Manifest format: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) with top-level manifest metadata and a list of artifact entries. Each entry includes path, size, sha256, chunk-hashes (optional), and jurisdiction tags.
- Proof signing: agent signs manifest using a per-agent keypair stored in the customer KMS; we will provide an optional Redwood verification flow where Redwood verifies signatures and stores only the manifest quorum (not content) in our ledger.
- Retention semantics: agent enforces retention via policy config; when jurisdiction prohibits a full snapshot, agent will only emit manifest with null content reference and a signed attestation explaining reason.

acceptance_criteria: Agent binary can be deployed in a customer VPC container and starts with provided config
Agent emits NDJSON manifest with signature and checksum for a minimum set of artifacts (config, service logs, runtime config)
Manifests can be uploaded to an S3 bucket with ObjectLock enabled and Redwood verifies the signature end-to-end
Agent honors jurisdictional retention flag: when region-blocked, content references are redacted but manifest attestation remains signed
Metrics exported to Prometheus endpoint: snapshot_duration_seconds, bytes_processed_total, failed_signature_count
Integration test demonstrating end-to-end: generate snapshot -> agent signs -> upload to test immutable store -> Redwood evidence-synthesizer ingests manifest and marks control as satisfied
